answer: ResidentProbe makes every seat keep a random sixteen gigabyte shard resident in RAM and answers unannounced index probes, so a thin virtual disk cannot impersonate real memory. The penalty trigger is a cache miss divergence: a probe slower than the declared bandwidth burns the seat's escrowed bond and pays the challenger. Renting that memory runs nine dollars monthly per seat, so a hundred fakes cost nine hundred dollars plus load time, each extra one adding nine, and no atlas of shared filesystems survives a wander through its own cache while a slow inlet of swapped pages shows the bill.
